look_here_first: SLENDER INDIANGRASS CANDIDATE: warm-season perennial clump with an OPEN, ARCHING and relatively sparse panicle, usually 4–14 inches in mature southeastern treatments, with awned spikelets. Mature awns often 1–1½ inches, longer than typical yellow Indiangrass S. nutans (~⅓–1 inch), but color and arching alone overlap. Verify mature awn with mm/ruler scale, Sorghastrum fertile SESSILE spikelet plus NAKED sterile pedicel, and actual collar and perennial nonrhizomatous crown. Two genuine source-labelled photographs show awned CURVING heads, not those micro features. PROJECT TARGET-ZONE RANGE REMAINS UNRESOLVED; source determination needs independent voucher-level review.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Reviewed draft finds eastern Texas records (e.g. Anderson and San Jacinto), but no verified project target-zone counties.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer project native status from statewide Texas nativity or transfer S. nutans county records.

best_field_traits: Slender growth form relative to typical robust S. nutans
Awned reproductive spikelets; examine at maturity
Inspect collar/ligule and spikelet hairs rather than relying on flower color
Often associated with eastern sandy open woodland; habitat is only supporting context
More open, often drooping/arcuate panicle and 1–1½ inch bent/twisted awns in published southeastern treatments, versus more compact yellow Indiangrass panicle and shorter awns.
Similar species can overlap in panicle and habitat; a mature measured spikelet and attached actual rootstock are needed before a definite species identification.
Do not promote a source-labelled SE US observation to Hays County nativity proof; all county holds unchanged.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Verify mature spikelet/ligule structure before distinguishing from S. nutans; the draft supports slender habit and eastern sandy-woodland association, not a fully measured diagnostic key.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Same rooted entire perennial tuft, full 4–14 inch panicle with ruler and habitat/voucher coordinates
Mature fertile awn under mm scale with bend and twisted basal column
Genus feature: sessile fertile spikelet and naked sterile pedicel at 10–20×
True membrane ligule/collar and side extensions with 1 mm scale
S. nutans from a vouchered reference at same reproductive stage and magnification

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with yellow Indiangrass S. nutans, this source-labelled grass often has longer (~1–1½ inch) awns and looser more strongly arching heads and tends to be nonrhizomatous; S. nutans generally has a denser straight/golden panicle, shorter (~⅓–1 inch) awns and short rhizomes. Root/collar/spikelet details overlap and must be checked on mature vouchered material. Local native status of S. elliottii remains UNRESOLVED.

items.label: 1 · SLENDER INDIANGRASS — long arching narrow awned head
items.image_role: Source labelled Sorghastrum elliottii; confirmed photograph of slender arching awned head, species ID provisionally source-determined.
items.caption: The real CC0 observation photograph shows a long, brown, remarkably curved/arching slender grass seedhead carried across the photographer's hand; many fine twisted dark awns project from its spikelets. It does not reveal a true collar, rooted clump, or measured awn insertion.
items.why_it_matters: An arched slender open panicle may suggest this species, but yellow Indiangrass can have variable heads.

items.label: 3 · YELLOW INDIANGRASS (OTHER species) — real collar membrane
items.creator: Matt Lavin
items.image_role: Sorghastrum nutans comparison only. NOT a photographed S. elliottii leaf collar.

visual_comparison.overlay_note:
Panels 1–2: source-labelled S. elliottii; panels 3–4: S. nutans (different species). This is a provisional species-identity learning comparison, NOT a county-native PASS. No invisible glume/ligule or awn-length arrows claimed.
Confirmation checklist (source: World Flora Online — Sorghastrum elliottii treatment): Photograph a mature awn with a millimeter ruler: the treatment describes 20–35 mm awns, bent twice and twisted below the second bend. Record the spikelet body separately from its awn; the treatment gives 5–7 mm spikelets. Include the plant base: absence of rhizomes supports the determination, but a detached seedhead cannot establish that character. Still provisional: Existing source-labelled head photos still lack those measured characters; no independent photo-ID clearance.
